items.why: The report gives "E2g1 383.33 (day 1) vs 385.83 (day 2), +2.50 cm-1; A1g 404.88 vs 407.31, +2.43 cm-1" and an unchanged separation "Delta = 21.56 ± 0.07 (day 1) and 21.47 ± 0.11 (day 2)".
It states "Si 519.98 vs 522.47, +2.49 cm-1", calls this "a spectrometer calibration drift and not a sample change", and treats Si as the fixed reference at 520.7 cm-1.
After Si referencing, "E2g1 and A1g agree within 0.02 ± 0.03 and -0.07 ± 0.12 cm-1", and the separation of "21.5 ± 0.1 cm-1, consistent with about 2L" holds on both days.

It says "There is no broadening of A1g, which is the usual signature of doping, and no splitting or broadening of E2g1, which would indicate strain", cites A1g softening and broadening under electron doping and -4.5 cm-1/% for E2g1 under strain, and reports unchanged widths.
It asks "Was the spectrometer recalibrated or the grating moved between days? ... Did you record a Si or Ne reference on each day?"

wrong_claims.why: The report rejects the idea outright: "The data give no sign of adsorbate-induced doping or strain."
It says "the layer number is the same" and "Crystal quality has not degraded."
